outlook: Grains are higher in overnight trade, with Minneapolis spring wheat up about 5 cents to $7.14 and all wheat contracts gaining as Russia and western Ukraine face dry soils ahead of winter wheat dormancy, though U.S. wheat export inspections are running 35% behind last year. Corn is back right at $5 after weekly inspections of 53.8 million bushels, and soybeans are up about 5 cents with inspections of 42 million bushels, well above the pace USDA needs. Monday's Crop Progress showed harvest behind normal after late-September rains, with corn 23% harvested (27% average) and soybeans 25% (33% average), and condition ratings slipped to 54% and 57% good-to-excellent. Canola is about flat, and USDA's WASDE and Crop Production reports come Friday.
